introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and Two outline maps of Cameroon.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions in all : question ONE (obligatoire, 31 marks), ONE question de la Section B et TWO de la Section C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum exprimable par section (B : 1 sur 2 ; C : 2 sur 4) ; la question 1 (Section A) est obligatoire donc sans règle ; la consigne complète (4 questions en tout) est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : Q1 = 31 (5+6+4+4+6+4+2), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 4+2+3+4+5+3+2 ; Q3 : 12+3+5+3 ; Q4 : 5+10+8 ; Q5 : 6+(8+3)+6 ; Q6 : 6+10+7 ; Q7 : 8+6+9), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, b, c ; Q5 b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

Sujet scanné de 5 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 7, carte topographique de Ndop avec sa légende, fond de carte du Cameroun) ; filigranes gcerevision.com ignorés. La carte (pivotée de 90 degrés sur la page, remise à l'endroit) et le fond de carte SONT dans le PDF et ont été recadrés en PNG ; le papier millimétré n'est pas fourni.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Contrast the climatic characteristics of the South Cameroon Low Plateau and that of the Adamawa plateau. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Approach.** Contrast point by point (a table scores well). The figures are approximate orders of magnitude.

| Characteristic | South Cameroon Low Plateau (e.g. around Yaounde) | Adamawa Plateau (e.g. around Ngaoundere) |
|---|---|---|
| Altitude | Low plateau, about 500 to 700 m | Higher plateau, about 1,000 to 1,500 m |
| Type of climate | Equatorial (Guinean) climate | Tropical (Sudan-Guinea) climate, modified by altitude |
| Rainfall total | Heavy, about 1,500 to 2,000 mm a year | Moderate to heavy, about 1,500 mm a year |
| Rainfall seasons | **Two rainy seasons** (about March to June and September to November) and two dry seasons (a short one in July to August and a longer one in December to February) | **One rainy season** (about April to October) and **one dry season** (November to March) |
| Temperature | Hot, about 23 to 25 degrees C mean, annual range small (2 to 3 degrees C) | Cooler, about 22 degrees C mean, with a larger annual and especially daily range (hot days and cool nights in the dry season) |
| Humidity and cloud | High humidity and cloud cover all year | Humid in the rainy season, drier air and clear sky in the dry season |
| Winds | Moist south-west monsoon, little wind | The dry, dusty harmattan (north-east trade wind) in the dry season |

**Explanation in one sentence each.** The South is near the equator and the sun is overhead twice a year (hence two rainy seasons), while the Adamawa is further north where the ITCZ passes only once, and its altitude lowers the temperature.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Discuss agricultural and energy resources as bases for industrialization in Cameroon. *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Industrialisation needs raw materials, power, capital, labour, transport and a market. Cameroon has a wide range of agricultural raw materials and a large energy potential, which are the two main bases for its industries.

**1. Agricultural resources (about 5 marks).**
- *Variety of raw materials* thanks to the climatic and relief diversity: cocoa and coffee (the south and the west), cotton (the north), sugar cane, rubber and oil palm, bananas and tea, timber, and cattle and fish.
- *Agro-industries:* the cotton gins and the textile mill (SODECOTON and CICAM in the north), the sugar complexes (SOSUCAM in the centre), the chocolate and the coffee processing, the rubber and palm oil factories (HEVECAM, SOCAPALM), the sawmills and plywood, brewing, the tea and banana plantations.
- *Advantages:* the raw materials are cheap and local, a large rural labour force, the products have an export market and the industries create jobs and added value.
- *Limits:* a large share is exported as raw material (cocoa, coffee, timber), with little value added; the production fluctuates with the weather and the world prices; transport of the crops is difficult.

**2. Energy resources (about 5 marks).**
- *Hydro-electric power* is the main source: the Sanaga river with the **Edea and Song Loulou** stations and the Lom Pangar reservoir, the Benue at **Lagdo**, and other sites on the Ntem (Memve'ele); this energy runs the **aluminium smelter (ALUCAM) at Edea**, and the industries in Douala and Yaounde.
- *Oil and gas:* the offshore fields near the Rio del Rey and the Douala-Kribi basin, the **SONARA refinery at Limbe**, the gas fields near Douala and the gas power plant at Kribi, and the pipeline for the Chad oil which ends at Kribi.
- *Advantages:* cheap hydropower, large undeveloped potential (the waterfalls and the heavy rainfall) and the export earnings of oil.
- *Limits:* the energy supply is unreliable (power cuts, seasonal low water levels, ageing transmission lines), the rural areas have little electricity, and the high cost of the dams.

**Conclusion.** Agricultural and energy resources have created a base for agro-processing and metallurgy, mostly in Douala, Edea and Yaounde, but their full use is limited by transport and electricity problems, the lack of capital and the competition from imports, so that industry contributes only a modest share to the national economy.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Explain THREE efforts that have been made to promote industrial growth in Cameroon. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Answer (three efforts, about 2 to 3 marks each, with explanation and an example).**
1. **Investment incentives and a favourable legal framework.** The Investment Code of the early 1990s, and later laws giving tax and customs incentives to investors, plus the creation of the **Industrial Free Zone regime** (export-oriented firms are exempt from many taxes), have attracted foreign and local firms.
2. **State participation and support to enterprises.** The government created public enterprises and institutions such as the **Société Nationale d'Investissement (SNI)** to invest in industries, and agencies to support small and medium enterprises (SMEs), together with credit and training.
3. **Improvement of infrastructure and energy.** The development of ports and roads (Douala port and the **Kribi industrial-port complex**), railways and electricity (the Sanaga and Lom Pangar dams, the Kribi gas power plant) reduces the cost of production and transport.
4. *Other acceptable efforts:* creation of industrial estates (Douala-Bassa, Bonaberi), the promotion of local processing of raw materials (a ban on exporting raw timber), the privatisation and restructuring of industries, vocational training and regional integration (CEMAC, which enlarges the market).
